title: Reading structured data
goals: Process a list of records consistently
Compute a total from named fields
Preserve record meaning while tracing a loop

prerequisite.prompt: Which key stores the occupied count in {"capacity": 8, "used": 3}?

vocabulary: One named part of a record
A variable updated to keep a running result

blocks.text: Two fictional cupboards are stored as a list of dictionaries. Each record uses the same keys and units. We want the total spare spaces. Treat the records as a dataset, and trace one record at a time before trusting a total.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
rows = [{"capacity": 8, "used": 3},
        {"capacity": 6, "used": 6}]
total = 0
for row in rows:
    spare = row["capacity"] - row["used"]
    total = total + spare
print(total)

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The loop variable row refers to each record in turn. We calculate spare from that record, then add it. total starts before the loop. An empty list produces 0 because there are no updates; it does not tell us whether no cupboards exist or records were not collected.

blocks.label: Add a third record with capacity 10 and used 4. Predict the total and list each contribution.

blocks.text: Putting total = 0 inside the loop discards earlier contributions. With the original rows it finishes at 0, the second contribution. Move the initialization before the loop and rerun both the original and reversed row order.
This loop assumes every record has the required integer fields. A missing used field causes KeyError. Do not silently treat a missing count as zero; that would invent unused capacity.

blocks.label: An empty dataset produces total 0. Can you conclude that every cupboard is full?

workbook.title: Read a row
workbook.prompt: In the worked dataset, state the number of records and the spare spaces in the second record.
workbook.answer: There are 2 records. The second has 0 spare spaces.

workbook.title: Trace all updates
workbook.prompt: For spare contributions 2, 4 and 1, trace total starting at 0.

workbook.title: Repair initialization
workbook.prompt: A loop resets total to 0 on each pass over contributions 2, 4, 1. What final total appears and how should it be fixed?
workbook.answer: It ends at 1. Initialize total once before the loop; repaired total 7.

workbook.title: Process new records independently
workbook.prompt: Write a loop for records (capacity 9, used 2), (capacity 5, used 1), and (capacity 4, used 4). Predict the total. Reverse the order and test an empty list.
workbook.answer: Contributions 7, 4, 0 give 11 in either order. Empty list gives 0. The loop must use both fields for every row.

workbook.title: Interpret an empty result
workbook.prompt: An empty dataset produces total 0. Can you conclude that every cupboard is full?
workbook.answer: No. No records were processed; the result provides no evidence about actual cupboards.

teacher.background: Teach Week 11 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. Two fictional cupboards are stored as a list of dictionaries. Each record uses the same keys and units. We want the total spare spaces. Treat the records as a dataset, and trace one record at a time before trusting a total. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.
materials: Python 3 editor with a fresh local practice file
Paper trace table and the student workbook
Fictional input records from this lesson; no real student identifiers
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and explain the purpose in the opening section.
Read the worked example and diagram; ask learners to trace each step aloud.
Complete W1 and W2, then compare predictions with observed results.
Collect the guided prediction before running; discuss a mismatch and its cause.
Retrieve the main rule without showing the previous answer.
Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Contributions 5, 0, 6; total 11. Exit: No. No records were processed; the result provides no evidence about actual cupboards.
